summary.intent: Execute all 9 plans of CipherBox Phase 71 (Share-Invite Security & IPNS Data-Integrity API) via wave-based parallel orchestration, then autonomously run the full post-execution ship pipeline (verify, secure, validate, simplify, SDK E2E gate, CodeRabbit review, PR creation, and PR-review resolution) without user babysitting.
summary.outcome: All 9 plans executed across 4 waves and merged with all gates green; phase verification passed 16/16 truths. The autonomous ship loop found and fixed two real regressions (a D-05 IPNS equivocation-guard bug via the SDK E2E gate, and a Greptile-flagged stale-write-key bug in the widen-only claim merge), triaged CodeRabbit/Greptile findings (several fixed in-diff, several deferred as todos), opened PR #599, and was mid-way through resolving a fresh batch of CodeRabbit PR-review threads when the transcript ends.

repo: This repo is squash-merge only (merge:false, rebase:false, squash:true, title=PR_TITLE) — individual commit subjects never reach main, so GSD executor's non-conventional 'feat 71-03:' style commits don't need rewording; only the PR title must be conventional and paren-free.
commitlint's subject-no-parens rule is enforced only via the pr-title.yml CI job on the PR title, not on individual commits.

CI's Migration Drift Check (ci.yml) only fails on structural drift (CREATE/DROP TABLE, ADD/DROP COLUMN, ALTER TYPE, RENAME COLUMN) via regex — it tolerates index/constraint name churn from TypeORM's migration:generate, so large generated diffs are often cosmetic noise.

Root cause of a real regression: apps/api/src/ipns/ipns.service.ts's D-05 same-seq CID-equivocation guard couldn't distinguish genuine equivocation from a forward-CAS attempt that lost a race; fix checks expectedSequenceNumber === embeddedSeq - 1 to fall through to the CAS UPDATE (409) instead of rejecting as equivocation (400).

apps/api/src/shares/share-invite.service.ts's widen-only claimInvite merge had a bug: a generation-bump via a write-capable invite onto an already-write-capable share advanced the read key/generation without re-wrapping encryptedWriteKey for the new generation, silently losing write access post-rotation.
gh pr edit fails on this repo due to Projects-classic GraphQL; PR body must be patched via `gh api -X PATCH repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/<N> -F body=@file`.
vitest (sdk-e2e) does not auto-load .env — SDK_E2E_SECRET must be passed explicitly or it silently falls back to a default that mismatches the API's TEST_LOGIN_SECRET, causing cascading 401s.
Throttling in apps/api is relaxed under NODE_ENV=test (app.module.ts:56), so a missing THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET doesn't cause 429s in that mode.

The API does not log handled 4xx responses; diagnosing a real 400 reason requires temporarily adding an axios response interceptor in packages/api-client/src/instance.ts, rebuilding the client chain, running the failing test, then reverting.
CodeRabbit CLI (`coderabbit review --agent --base main --type committed`) skips diffs over 150 changed files.
gsd-tools' commit helper can report commit_failed while the commit actually lands — must verify via `git log --oneline -1`, never blindly retry.

code.finding: D-05 same-seq CID equivocation guard threw 400 even when embeddedSeq===dbSeq resulted from a legitimate forward-CAS race (expectedSequenceNumber===embeddedSeq-1); fixed to fall through to the CAS UPDATE producing 409 in that case.

claimInvite's widen-only merge left encryptedWriteKey wrapped for the old generation when a generation-bump landed via a write-capable invite on an already-write-capable share; fixed to re-wrap/advance the write key together with the generation bump. Also added a pre-transaction validation rejecting a write-capable invite claimed without an encryptedWriteKey (CodeRabbit MAJOR + Greptile P1 signal).
Permission-derivation used `!== null` on a string|null|undefined DTO field, misclassifying undefined write keys; loosened to `!= null` in both occurrences per CodeRabbit finding #10.

Added composite indexes on shares/share_invites keyed by share_root_ipns_name per CodeRabbit N1; required matching @Index decorators on Share and ShareInvite entities to avoid Migration Drift Check false-positive.

workflow: When multiple parallel subagents share a worktree-per-plan execution model, verify each worktree exists (and its config.lock is released) before dispatching the next agent in the same wave, to avoid a git config race.

Don't trust an executor subagent's own test/check output blindly when diagnostics (e.g. LSP/tsc errors) surface — re-verify against the actual merged tree at the post-merge gate rather than the in-worktree report.

When a live-stack human-verify checkpoint plan pauses, inspect existing running processes (e.g. a stale `node dist/main.js` on the target port) before reusing them — stale builds can produce false negatives.
Use a background poll with correct tab-delimited parsing for `gh pr checks` (a naive awk split on spaces breaks because check names like 'CodeRabbit / Review' contain spaces).
Second-reviewer signal (Greptile P1 + CodeRabbit MAJOR both flagging the same class of issue) is a valid reason to reverse an earlier 'defer' triage decision and fix immediately.

Before committing to a 'defer as todo' triage decision, check whether the fix is actually cheap (e.g. entity @Index annotations, controller @ApiResponse codes) — several items initially deferred were reclassified as low-risk fixes once inspected.

friction: CodeRabbit's PR-level review took long enough to appear pending/skipped that the agent initially misdiagnosed it as skipped, prompting a user correction ('coderabbit review is in - not skipped was just taking a while').

A local DB reset (done to get a clean IPNS unique-constraint state for Test 21) had the side effect of wiping tee_key_state, causing 2 unrelated tee-republish test failures that had to be diagnosed and confirmed environmental rather than a regression.
First poll script for `gh pr checks` had a parsing bug (awk splitting on spaces broke on multi-word check names), requiring a second corrected poll.

The generic regression/test gate in the workflow defaults to `npm test`, which is wrong for this pnpm monorepo and risks RAM-starving infra-dependent suites — had to be manually overridden each time with scoped, correct commands.
CodeRabbit's finding #5 (SECURITY.md wording) and #6 (owner-reconcile hex format) were false positives requiring verification effort before being dismissed.
